## The five claims

**1. "Reduces to exactly a finite Zariski atlas" — TRUE on types, MISLEADING on cost.**

The type match is genuine, not a restatement. `Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:58-60` defines `pic0TypeFunctor` as a `noncomputable abbrev` for `(pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat` — literally the spelling `JacobianData.rep` is typed against at `JacobianData.lean:93`. `JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy` (`JacobianDataCharts.lean:71`) sets `rep := rep` with no transport. `ofCharts` (`:182`) carries only the three frozen hypotheses. **2. `GeometricallyReduced` redundancy — VERIFIED, both halves.** `Curve/GeometricallyReduced.lean:130` and `:140` are both `instance (priority := 100)`. Independently computed chain into `Pic0SigmaSheaf`'s closure: `Pic0SigmaSheaf → PicEtCoverBridge → Pic0ZariskiSheaf → Pic0Functor → PicEtMap → PicEtMapToolkit → PicEtAffZariskiGlue → PicEtAffZariskiSep → RelPicPi → ProjectionUnits → Separatedness → UniversalSections → Curve.GeometricallyReduced`. **4. §7.3 vs ADDENDUM 4 — NOT the same claim, and §7.3's "over any field" is unproven.** Filed as **I-0367**.

They are different witnesses. ADDENDUM 4 §4.3 (`spec-dd-r.md:809-838`) uses the universal divisor over `T = Sym^g C`, irreducibility coming from the finite surjection `C × Sym^{g−1}C → C × Sym^g C`. §7.3 (`w4-rep-critical-path.md:226-234`) uses a *pencil*: the graph of a degree-`g` map `φ : C → P¹`, so `supp D = φ⁻¹(U)` is literally an open of `C`. That needs no `Sym^g` — genuinely cheaper, and a real contribution. But it is a new result, not corroboration.

The shrink-stability step you flagged is **fine** in both: a nonempty open of an irreducible space is irreducible hence connected, and under the graph reading "an open subscheme of the irreducible `C`" is literally correct. That is not where it breaks. It breaks on residue degrees:

> §7.3 writes the divisor `s₀ + s_∞` and computes `ℓ(K − s₀ − s_∞) ≥ g − 2`, i.e. it treats `s₀, s_∞` as **degree-1 points**. Over `𝔽₂` with `g = 2`, `e₀ = e₁ = 2`, §7.3's witness does not exist.

That is precisely the regime ADDENDUM 4 §4.4's "only if" isolates. 210	`Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:79` declares `variable [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]` before the sheaf
211	theorem and `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`, and `Challenge.lean:96-98`'s frozen bundle does not
212	supply it — so the whole representability seam appeared to demand a hypothesis the target forbids.
213	It does not. `Curve/GeometricallyReduced.lean:130` gives `Smooth.geometricallyReduced` and `:140`
214	gives `Smooth.of_smoothOfRelativeDimension_one`, both instances, and that module is in
215	`Pic0SigmaSheaf`'s import closure. The hypothesis is redundant, not a gap. Machine-checked record:
216	`Picard/JacobianDataCharts.lean:210`.
217	
218	### 7.3 §2's "one open experiment" was already answered, by this file's own sibling
219	
220	§2 closes with *"At `g ≥ 2` no witness has ever been exhibited… It is not acceptable to keep
221	planning without knowing which."* That question was settled in the **same round**:
222	`informal/spec-dd-r.md` **ADDENDUM 4** (commit `d7e8348ce`) is titled *"the on-stratum witness
223	EXISTS"*, and roadmap leaf `…ddr.certificate.field-size` is `done` carrying the sharp theorem.
224	Independently re-derived this round, and it agrees:
225	
226	> For any `g ≥ 2`, take a pencil of degree `g` on `C` one of whose members is a divisor
227	> `E ≥ s₀ + s_∞` with `π(s₀) = 0`, `π(s_∞) = ∞`. Such an `E` exists: `ℓ(E) = 1 + ℓ(K − E)`, so any
228	> `E` with `s₀ + s_∞ ≤ E ≤ K'` for a canonical `K' ≥ s₀ + s_∞` has `ℓ(E) ≥ 2`; and such a `K'`
229	> exists because `ℓ(K − s₀ − s_∞) ≥ g − 2 ≥ 1` for `g ≥ 3`, and for `g = 2` exactly when `s_∞` is
230	> the hyperelliptic conjugate of `s₀` (which one is free to arrange, since `π` is a choice: a
231	> function with a zero at `s₀` and a pole at `s_∞` is a finite map sending them to `0` and `∞`).
232	> The support of the total family is an open subscheme of the irreducible `C`, hence irreducible,
233	> hence **connected after every Zariski shrink of the base** — which is exactly why the shrink
234	> evasion that kills the `g = 1` case does not apply here.
235	
236	So: **the fixed-pair certificate route is dead on the campaign's own stratum**, over any field.
237	Do not re-run this experiment. Do not formalise the witness either — ADDENDUM 4 §4.5 explains why
238	(it needs `Sym^g C` / `Hilb^g`, and this tree constructs no curve other than `P¹`).

240	### 7.4 The live strategic question is R1 versus R2, and it is not "which is cheaper"
241	
242	With the fixed pair dead, `spec-dd-r` ADDENDUM 4 §4.4 leaves exactly two repairs, and they differ
243	in kind, not only in cost:
244	
245	* **R1** (`p1-aut` → `fibre-avoid` → `cert-relocalize`): let the certificate quantify over a twist
246	  `γ ∈ Aut(P¹_k)`. Proved correct **iff `|P¹(k)| ≥ g + 2`** — i.e. over every infinite field and

8	/-!
9	# The Jacobian representability datum (Wave-4 seam D1, `JacobianData`)
10	
11	The pinned representability datum for the degree-zero étale-sheafified relative Picard
12	functor `pic0Functor C` of the challenge curve: a representing object `J`, an honest
13	`Functor.RepresentableBy` datum (no `Nonempty`, no choice), and the two construction
14	certificates (`LocallyOfFiniteType`, `QuasiCompact`).  This is the frozen Wave-4
15	interface shape (`informal/w4-datum-worksheet.md` §1.1, verbatim), together with the
16	design-§5 consumers `grpObj` / `homEquiv` / `uniqueUpToIso` — and nothing else.
17	
18	## Ownership split (binding, w5-worksheet D1)
19	
20	* The **producer** `jacobianData C : JacobianData C`, the quasi-compactness certificate,
21	  and the discharge of the frozen `Jacobian`/`instGrpObj` sorries of `Challenge.lean`
22	  are **DAT-J property** (the parallel Wave-4 fleet).  None of them lives here.
23	* This file is the **Wave-5/6/7 consumption interface**: downstream files take
24	  `(d : JacobianData C)` as a section variable, activate the group structure per proof
25	  via `letI := d.grpObj` (or `attribute [local instance] JacobianData.grpObj`), and
26	  phrase every statement about `d.J`.  At DAT-J discharge time the frozen gate
27	  instantiates them by `exact theorem_x … (jacobianData C)` — definitionally, since
28	  `Jacobian C := (jacobianData C).J`.
29	* Extensions to this file are **additive only**; the structure shape never changes.
30	
31	## The `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage
32	
33	`rep` is typed against `(pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat`
34	so that mathlib's `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` applies **verbatim** with
35	`F := pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat`.  The functor value at a test `T` is
36	*definitionally* the coerced subgroup `↥(pic0Subgroup C T)`; `homEquiv` and
37	`homEquiv_comp` below own this defeq once, exposing the equivalence against
38	`pic0Subgroup C T` and the naturality against `pic0Map` — no consumer ever meets the
39	`forget₂ ⋙ forget` spelling again.
40	
41	## η-defeq verdict (recon §5 "lower-order unknown", RECORDED)
42	
43	**POSITIVE, with one keying caveat.**  `Over.mk d.J.hom` is definitionally equal to
44	`d.J` (structure-eta for `Comma`/`CostructuredArrow` plus unit-like eta for the
45	`Discrete PUnit` right leg): the ascription
46	`(d.grpObj : GrpObj (Over.mk d.J.hom))` elaborates as-is, so **no transport lemma is
47	ever needed**.  Caveat: bare instance *search* does not unfold `Over.mk` on its own,
48	so a consumer of `smooth_of_grpObj` — whose group hypothesis is `[GrpObj (Over.mk f)]`
49	at `f := d.J.hom` — must key the instance at the `Over.mk` spelling:
50	`letI : GrpObj (Over.mk d.J.hom) := d.grpObj` (pure defeq, zero cost; mathlib itself
51	uses the same ascription idiom in `Group/Smooth.lean`).  Instances stated directly on
52	`G : Over (Spec (.of K))` (e.g. `IsClosedImmersion η[G].left`) fire on `d.J` with no
53	massage at all.  The `example`-level smoke tests at the bottom of this file are the
54	machine-checked record; the T-chain (tangent lane) and S2 (`Smooth` via
55	`smooth_of_grpObj`) may rely on this freely.
56	
57	## Main declarations
58	
59	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData C` — the frozen datum structure.
60	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.grpObj` — the group-object structure on `d.J` via
61	  `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` (the discharge route of the frozen `instGrpObj`).
62	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.homEquiv` / `homEquiv_comp` — the universal property
63	  in consumer form: `(T ⟶ d.J) ≃ pic0Subgroup C T`, natural against `pic0Map`.
64	* `AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianData.uniqueUpToIso` / `homEquiv_uniqueUpToIso_hom` — any
65	  two data have canonically isomorphic representing objects (Wave-7's `baseChangeIso`
66	  mechanism), with the intertwining property.

79	
80	/-- **The pinned representability datum** for the degree-zero étale-sheafified relative
81	Picard functor of the curve `C` (w4-datum-worksheet §1.1, frozen).  Produced once, by
82	explicit construction, in Wave 4 (DAT-J: `jacobianData`); consumed as a section
83	variable everywhere else.  NEVER a sorried instance, NEVER `Nonempty` + choice.
84	
85	The typing of `rep` is chosen so that `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` applies verbatim with
86	`F := pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat` (see `JacobianData.grpObj`). -/
87	structure JacobianData (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
88	    [IsProper C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
89	    Type (u + 1) where
90	  /-- The representing object (the Jacobian-to-be). -/
91	  J : Over (Spec (.of k))
92	  /-- The pinned universal datum: `Hom(T, J) ≃ Pic⁰(T)`, naturally in the test `T`. -/
93	  rep : ((pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat).RepresentableBy J
94	  /-- Certificate from the construction (Kleiman 4.8(1) shape); NOT re-derived via the

96	  locallyOfFiniteType : LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom
97	  /-- Certificate from the construction (a posteriori: `|J|` is the image of a
98	  quasi-compact divisor scheme under the Abel map).  Feeds `IsProper` (Wave 5) via
99	  `finite type = qc + lft`. -/

101	
102	namespace JacobianData
103	
104	variable {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
105	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
106	
107	/-- The group-object structure on the representing object, via mathlib's
108	`GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` — this is the (definitional) discharge route of the frozen
109	`Jacobian.instGrpObj`.  Not a global instance here (the datum is a section variable);
110	activate per proof with `letI := d.grpObj` or
111	`attribute [local instance] JacobianData.grpObj`. -/
112	@[implicit_reducible]

114	  GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy d.J (pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) d.rep
115	
116	/-- **The universal property, consumer form**: morphisms into `d.J` are degree-zero
117	étale Picard classes.  This accessor owns the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` defeq massage once:
118	the target is the honest subgroup carrier `pic0Subgroup C T`. -/
119	def homEquiv (d : JacobianData C) {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} :
120	    (T ⟶ d.J) ≃ pic0Subgroup C T :=
121	  d.rep.homEquiv
122	
123	/-- Naturality of `homEquiv` against the degree-zero restriction maps `pic0Map`
124	(element form of the `RepresentableBy` naturality, with the functor value unfolded
125	through `forget₂ ⋙ forget`). -/
126	theorem homEquiv_comp (d : JacobianData C) {T T' : Over (Spec (.of k))}
127	    (f : T' ⟶ T) (g : T ⟶ d.J) :
128	    d.homEquiv (f ≫ g) = pic0Map C f (d.homEquiv g) :=
129	  d.rep.homEquiv_comp f g
130	
131	/-- Representing objects are unique up to isomorphism (mathlib
132	`Functor.RepresentableBy.uniqueUpToIso`): any two Jacobian data for the same curve have
133	canonically isomorphic `J`.  This is Wave-7's `baseChangeIso` mechanism. -/
134	noncomputable def uniqueUpToIso (d d' : JacobianData C) : d.J ≅ d'.J :=
135	  d.rep.uniqueUpToIso d'.rep
136	
137	/-- The intertwining property of `uniqueUpToIso`: composing with the canonical
138	isomorphism commutes with the two universal properties. -/
139	theorem homEquiv_uniqueUpToIso_hom (d d' : JacobianData C) {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}
140	    (f : T ⟶ d.J) :
141	    d'.homEquiv (f ≫ (d.uniqueUpToIso d').hom) = d.homEquiv f := by
142	  have h : (d.uniqueUpToIso d').hom = d'.rep.homEquiv.symm (d.rep.homEquiv (𝟙 d.J)) := rfl
143	  rw [homEquiv, homEquiv, h, Functor.RepresentableBy.comp_homEquiv_symm]
144	  exact (d'.rep.homEquiv.apply_symm_apply _).trans (d.rep.homEquiv_eq f).symm
145	
146	end JacobianData

149	registered)
150	
151	The first test records that `Over.mk d.J.hom ≡ d.J` definitionally (structure eta); the
152	second that instance resolution crosses it — `smooth_of_grpObj`'s hypothesis
153	`[GrpObj (Over.mk f)]` at `f := d.J.hom` is discharged by `letI := d.grpObj`; the third
154	that mathlib's `IsClosedImmersion η[d.J].left` instance fires on `d.J` as-is.  T-chain
155	and S2 depend on these; if a mathlib bump ever breaks them, a transport lemma must be
156	added HERE, not in the consumers. -/
157	
158	section EtaDefeqSmokeTests

163	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
164	
165	/-- Smoke test 1: `Over.mk d.J.hom` is definitionally `d.J` — the ascription
166	elaborates with no transport. -/
167	noncomputable example (d : JacobianData C) : GrpObj (Over.mk d.J.hom) := d.grpObj
168	
169	/-- Smoke test 2: `smooth_of_grpObj` applies to `d.J.hom` with no transport lemma;
170	the group instance must be *keyed* at `Over.mk d.J.hom` (the ascribed `letI` below —
171	instance search does not unfold `Over.mk` on its own, but the ascription is pure
172	defeq). -/
173	example (d : JacobianData C) [GeometricallyReduced d.J.hom] : Smooth d.J.hom :=
174	  letI := d.locallyOfFiniteType
175	  letI : GrpObj (Over.mk d.J.hom) := d.grpObj
176	  smooth_of_grpObj d.J.hom
177	
178	/-- Smoke test 3: the unit section of `d.J` is a closed immersion (mathlib's
179	group-scheme instance fires on `d.J` directly, with the datum's group structure in
180	scope). -/
181	example (d : JacobianData C) [GrpObj d.J] : IsClosedImmersion η[d.J].left :=
182	  inferInstance
183	
184	end EtaDefeqSmokeTests
185	
186	end AlgebraicGeometry

/-! ## The Σ-extension as a presheaf on the big site -/

/-- **The big-site carrier of the slice trick**: the Σ-extension of the type-valued
degree-zero Picard functor, `T ↦ Σ (a : T ⟶ Spec k), pic⁰(Over.mk a)`.  Reducible so
that the stage-2 `sigmaExtension` calculus applies syntactically. -/
noncomputable abbrev pic0SigmaFunctor : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
  Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (pic0TypeFunctor C)

variable [GeometricallyReduced C.hom]

set_option maxHeartbeats 800000 in
-- The amalgamation seams unify the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage of `pic0Functor`
-- against the Σ-extension calculus by unfolding; within the DAT-2/PicEtMap 1600000
-- precedent.
/-- **The big-site Zariski sheaf certificate of the Σ-extension** (DAT-6 keystone,
worksheet §1.2 site gap 1): mathlib's reduction collapses the sheaf condition to
elementwise ∃!-amalgamation on honest open covers, where the Σ-components glue by
`Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms` and the fibre components by the stage-1 evaluation
bridge. -/
theorem pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf :
    Presieve.IsSheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology (pic0SigmaFunctor C) := by
  rw [Precoverage.isSheaf_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderBaseChange]
  intro Y S hS
  obtain ⟨𝓤, rfl⟩ := Scheme.exists_cover_of_mem_pretopology hS
  rw [Presieve.isSheafFor_arrows_iff]
  intro x hx
  -- glue the Σ-components along the scheme-level cover
  have hpair : ∀ i j, pullback.fst (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j) ≫ (x i).1
      = pullback.snd (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j) ≫ (x j).1 := fun i j =>
    congrArg Sigma.fst
      (hx i j (pullback (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j)) (pullback.fst _ _) (pullback.snd _ _)
        pullback.condition)
  obtain ⟨aY, ha⟩ : ∃ aY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k), ∀ i, 𝓤.f i ≫ aY = (x i).1 :=
    ⟨𝓤.glueMorphisms (fun i => (x i).1) hpair,
      fun i => 𝓤.ι_glueMorphisms (fun i => (x i).1) hpair i⟩
  -- the induced slice cover of `Over.mk aY` and its member sections
  haveI hop : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion
      ((Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)).left :=
    fun i => 𝓤.map_prop i
  have hcov : ∀ p : (Over.mk aY).left, ∃ i, p ∈ Scheme.Hom.opensRange
      ((Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)).left := by
    intro p
    obtain ⟨i, y, hy⟩ := 𝓤.exists_eq p
    exact ⟨i, y, hy⟩
  -- the fibre components are a compatible family on the slice cover
  have hcompat : ∀ (i j : 𝓤.I₀) (Z : Over (Spec (.of k)))
      (gi : Z ⟶ Over.mk ((x i).1)) (gj : Z ⟶ Over.mk ((x j).1)),
      gi ≫ (Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)
          = gj ≫ (Over.homMk (𝓤.f j) (ha j) : Over.mk ((x j).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY) →
      pic0Map C gi ((x i).2) = pic0Map C gj ((x j).2) := by
    intro i j Z gi gj hg
    have hleft : gi.left ≫ 𝓤.f i = gj.left ≫ 𝓤.f j := congrArg Over.Hom.left hg
    have hdesc := Over.map_eq_of_sigmaExtension_map_eq gi gj

* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf` / **`pic0SigmaSheaf C`**: the sheaf

  compatibility descent (`map_eq_of_sigmaExtension_map_eq`).

  Σ-extension by the glued scheme, and the stage-2 Σ-descent `overSlice` turns it

759	
760	ADDENDUM 3's second corrigendum left one question: the no-go's argument is degree-agnostic, but
761	its only exhibited witness (`F = tX² + XY + tY²` over `k[t]`, `C = P¹`, `π = id`) has degree 2 on a
762	curve of genus 0, off the stratum the functor pins. At `g = 0` the no-go is vacuous, at `g = 1`
763	the base can be shrunk to confine, and at `g ≥ 2` nobody had exhibited anything. This addendum
764	settles it, corrects the argument ADDENDUM 3 used for shrink-stability, and — the part that
765	actually decides the route — gives a sharp iff for R1.
766	
767	### 4.1 First, the criterion ADDENDUM 3 used is the wrong one
768	
769	ADDENDUM 3 argued shrink-stability as "the divisor stays irreducible over every nonempty open of
770	the base, so no Zariski shrink evades the no-go". That is true of the exhibited family and it is
771	not the right criterion, because `IsLocallyCertified` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyZar.lean:71`) asks for
772	a **span-⊤ family**, i.e. a *cover* — and a cover cannot delete a point. The correct criterion is
773	
774	> (★) there is a point `s ∈ Spec R` such that for **every** open `U ∋ s`, some connected component
775	> of `supp(D|_U)` meets both `π⁻¹(p₀)` and `π⁻¹(p₁)`.
776	
777	Under the criterion ADDENDUM 3 actually stated, the campaign's own genus-0 example would be
778	*evaded*: the two witness points of `tX² + XY + tY²` are `([1:0], 0)` and `([0:1], 0)`, both lying
779	over `t = 0`, and over `t ≠ 0` the roots are `(−1 ± √(1−4t²))/2t`, which are never `0` or `∞`. So
780	`D` restricted to `𝔸¹ ∖ {0}` misses *both* pinned fibres. It is a genuine counterexample only
781	because a cover must contain `t = 0`. The conclusion was right; half the reason was missing.
782	
783	### 4.2 The reduction (general — no hypotheses on `k`, `C`, `π`, `n`)
784	
785	Let `S = supp D ⊆ C ×_k Spec R`. Since `D` is finite flat of degree `n` over `R`, `S → Spec R` is
786	finite, hence closed. For `c ∈ P¹(k)` set `W_c :=` the image in `Spec R` of `S ∩ (π⁻¹(c) × Spec R)`
787	— a closed subset. Then for `s ∈ Spec R`:
788	
789	* `s ∉ W_c` ⟹ `U := Spec R ∖ W_c` is an open neighbourhood of `s` on which `supp(D|_U)` misses
790	  `π⁻¹(c)` entirely, i.e. `D|_U` is confined to the chart complementary to `π⁻¹(c)`;
791	* `s ∈ W_c` ⟹ *every* `U ∋ s` has `supp(D|_U)` meeting `π⁻¹(c)`.
792	
793	And `s ∈ W_c ⟺ supp(D_s)` meets `π⁻¹(c)`, a purely **fibrewise** condition. Since `D_s` is finite
794	of degree `n` over `κ(s)`, the image of `supp(D_s)` in `|P¹_k|` has **at most `n` closed points**.
795	
796	Two consequences worth stating separately.
797	
798	**(A) Necessity of `g ≥ 2`.** A witness needs one `s` whose fibre meets both `π⁻¹(p₀)` and
799	`π⁻¹(p₁)`, hence `n ≥ 2`. At `n = g = 1`, `W_{p₀} ∩ W_{p₁} = ∅`, so
800	`{Spec R ∖ W_{p₀}, Spec R ∖ W_{p₁}}` is a *confining cover*. That is I-0356's `g = 1` verdict, now
801	with a proof rather than an observation.
802	
803	**(B) Connectedness is the second half.** The two witness points must lie in the same connected
804	component of `supp(D|_U)` for every `U ∋ s` — equivalently in the same connected component of
805	`S ×_R O_{R,s}`, idempotents of a finite algebra descending to a finite level. Reducible
806	constructions therefore fail: if `S = Δ ∪ ({b} × T)`, a certifier just shrinks until the

809	### 4.3 The witness, over an arbitrary field
810	
811	Hypotheses: `k` **any** field; `C/k` smooth proper geometrically irreducible of genus `g ≥ 2`;
812	`π : C → P¹` any finite dominant map; `p₀ ≠ p₁ ∈ P¹(k)` the pinned pair.
813	
814	1. `Div^g_{C/k} ≅ Sym^g C =: T` exists over `k` — smooth projective, geometrically irreducible of

816	   finite flat of degree `g` over `T` (Kleiman, *The Picard scheme*, FGA Explained §9.3; BLR
817	   §8.2/9.3). Every degree-`g` relative divisor over every `R` is a pullback of `D_univ`, so this
818	   analysis is exhaustive rather than a lucky example.
819	2. **`supp D_univ` is irreducible over any `k`**: it is the image of the finite surjection
820	   `C × Sym^{g−1}C → C × Sym^g C`, `(x, ξ) ↦ (x, x + ξ)`, and `C × Sym^{g−1}C` is irreducible

831	5. **Non-confinability.** Let `{D(g_i)}` be any span-⊤ family. Some `D(g_i)` contains `s`. Then
832	   `supp(D|_{D(g_i)})` is a nonempty open of the irreducible `supp D_univ`, hence irreducible,

839	
840	**Field dependence: none.** It works over `F₂`, over imperfect fields, over non-closed fields.
841	Enlarging `k` does not escape it and neither does descent from a large field — the witness is
842	already there over the small field.

845	
846	The reduction in §4.2 gives, with the pinned pair allowed to vary per cover member (which is
847	exactly what R1 buys):
848	
849	> **R1 is correct if and only if `|P¹(k)| ≥ n + 2`.**

852	> choose `c ∈ P¹(k)` outside it and any `c' ≠ c`. Then `U := Spec R ∖ W_c` confines `D|_U` to the
853	> chart complementary to `π⁻¹(c)`. Doing this at every `s` gives a Zariski cover on which the

856	> *Only if.* If `Σ_{c ∈ P¹(k)} e_c ≤ n`, where `e_c` is the minimal degree of a closed point of `C`
857	> over `c` (e.g. `q + 1 ≤ g` when `C` has a rational point over each `c`), take
858	> `ξ_s = Σ_c q_c + padding`. Then `s ∈ W_c` for **every** `c ∈ P¹(k)`, and no pinned pair confines.
